_comment: Settings of the front end (read by Vite and by the browser code). No code here. Decisions: D17 (no hardcoded paths), D19 (dev badge), D22 (MapLibre GL JS).

screenshots._comment: Read by frontend/tools/screenshots.mjs (a real browser in Docker). The base URL and the output folder come from the environment variables named here.

design_shots._comment: Read by frontend/tools/design_shots.mjs (PLAN-007 step 9.5): screenshots of the finished page at these window widths (px) with one place chosen, for the user's look. Same environment variables as the screenshots block. 'tall' = a second shot of the whole plan column.

browser_checks._comment: Read by frontend/tools/browser_checks.mjs (step 8 done-check: the plan page in real browsers). Environment variables name the site, the screenshot folder, the engine (chromium, firefox or webkit) and an optional computer-installed browser (msedge).

map._comment: Plan PLAN-007 (decisions D29, D31). start = the globe the page opens with; fly = where a chosen place is shown: the globe flies there and flattens (the projection morphs from a globe at morph_from_zoom to a flat map at fly.zoom, then the flight goes on to zoom_by_source: the device location lands closest, D35). With 'reduce motion' set in the system the view jumps. start_model = which model the map shows first (ifs, aifs-single or both).

key._comment: The titled colour key under the map (PLAN-012): plain words for every colour. {mm} is filled from the manifest (the rain threshold of the agreement view). Words only; the colours come from the manifest and the colour scale.
key.title: What the colours mean

agreement.both_wet: Bright blue: both models say rain
agreement.disagree: Dim blue: only one model says rain
agreement.none: No colour: neither model says rain
agreement.footnote: Rain here means {mm} mm or more in a 6-hour block.

key.model: Blue is a little rain, green and yellow more, orange and red a lot. The colours show rain only, not temperature.

basemap._comment: The stored base map (PLAN-010, D38): an OpenStreetMap extract served from our own site, below data_url_path + url_prefix. file, assets_dir, sprite_set and flavor must equal config/pipeline.toml (basemap_file, basemap_assets_dir) and config/basemap.toml (style_assets.sprite_dir, sprite_flavor); a test checks. attribution_html is shown on the map (the OpenStreetMap licence asks for it); only https links are allowed there (a test checks).

colours._comment: Brighter place names, borders and road names than the style's dark defaults (#3d3d3d to #7a7a7a on land #1f1f1f were too dim to read; user feedback, D39). Keys are fields of the dark flavor of @protomaps/basemaps (a test checks the names); every label colour must keep a contrast of at least 7 : 1 with the land colour (a test measures it).

basemap.attribution_html: © OpenStreetMap contributors, Protomaps

live._comment: The browser-side drawing of the rain at screen sharpness (PLAN-009, D35): used on the flat map from min_zoom up; below it, and on the globe, the pre-made pictures are shown. canvas_scale = picture pixels per screen pixel (0.5: each picture pixel covers 2 x 2 screen pixels, smoothed by the browser); lut_size = steps of the continuous colour ramp; agreement_soft_steps = half the width, in 0.1 mm storage steps, over which the agreement fades around the plan's threshold; fade_from_mm must equal frames.fade_from_mm in config/backend.toml (a test checks); max_tiles = most tiles fetched for one view, above it the pre-made picture is used; debounce_ms = wait after the last map move before drawing.

geocoder._comment: Place search (decision D27): Open-Meteo geocoding. ONLY the typed text and the visitor's IP address go to this host; its origin is the single outside host in connect-src of config/headers.conf (a test keeps the two in step). Search runs only when the visitor presses Enter or the button.

reverse_geocoder._comment: Names the DEVICE position (decision D32): BigDataCloud free client-side reverse geocoding (the documented host api.bigdatacloud.net answers 307 to api-bdc.io, which is the host used here, E030), made for calls from the visitor's browser with the device's own location. Only the position and the visitor's IP address go to this host; its origin is the second and last outside host in connect-src of config/headers.conf (a test keeps the two in step). Not used for clicks on the map.

freshness._comment: The honesty strip (PLAN-013 step 13.1, D9): the page warns in plain words when the forecast run is older than max_age_hours. ECMWF's 00z and 12z runs (the only ones with the 240 h IFS files) appear about 7.5 h after their time and a new one comes every 12 h, so the run shown is normally 8 to 21 hours old; 30 h means a whole run was missed. A test keeps it at 24 or more.

The data was changed: ECMWF's accumulated rain is turned into amounts for 6-hour blocks (millimetres, rounded to 0.1 mm), the two models are compared, and the result is shown as rain levels, maps and plans.

This is not an official weather warning. For warnings, use your national weather service.

plan_levels._comment: Colours of the four rain levels in the day view (PLAN-011 step 11.3), one entry per level id of config/activities.json. bar = the top bar and the drops (the colours follow the map's rain ramp: blue, yellow, red); bg = the dark tile; text = the words. A test checks every text/background pair (WCAG AA 4.5 : 1), the bar against the tile (3 : 1) and that the four are distinct. Colour is never the only signal: the word, the drops and the tick say the same.

check._comment: Read by frontend/tools/plan_check.mjs (checks the browser code on the real exported tiles against the reference made by scripts/plan_reference.py) and by scripts/level_shares.py (level_share_days = how many days of the newest run it counts). Same files as config/pipeline.toml [paths] site_dir and plan_reference_file.

colour_scale._comment: Colour for a value at or above the first number of each pair; below the first stop the pixel is transparent. Used by the export (backend/export.py) for the map frames and by the page for the legend.
